defs.d: To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something
defs.ex: Enjoy your holidays!   I enjoy dancing.

defs.d: To have the use or benefit of something.
defs.ex: I plan to go travelling while I still enjoy good health.

defs.d: The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
The food or money required to keep someone alive and healthy; one's support, maintenance.
defs.ex: He works as a cobbler's apprentice for his keep.

defs.d: To continue in (a course or mode of action); not to intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.
defs.ex: to keep silence;  to keep one's word;  to keep possession

defs.d: (heading) To hold the status of something.
Someone who lives in modern times.
Pertaining to a current or recent time and style; not ancient.
defs.ex: Our online interactive game is a modern approach to teaching about gum disease.  Although it was built in the 1600s, the building still has a very modern look.

defs.d: (history) Pertaining to the modern period (c.1800 to contemporary times), particularly in academic historiography.
To bring (a system, etc.) online; to promote to an active or running state.
Of a system: connected (generally electrically) to a larger network.
Available over, or delivered from, the Internet.
defs.ex: I prefer to read online newspapers.

defs.d: While online; while in a running or active state, or connected to the Internet.
defs.ex: He works online.

defs.d: Used as plural of person; a body of human beings considered generally or collectively; a group of two or more persons.
defs.ex: There were so many people at the restaurant last night.

defs.d: Persons forming or belonging to a particular group, such as a nation, class, ethnic group, country, family, etc.
To stock with people or inhabitants; to fill as with people; to populate.
To become populous or populated.
An individual; usually a human being.
defs.ex: Each person is unique, both mentally and physically.

defs.d: The physical body of a being seen as distinct from the mind, character, etc.
A food made primarily of a mixture of raw or cold ingredients, typically vegetables, usually served with a dressing such as vinegar or mayonnaise.
A raw vegetable of the kind used in salads.
(authorship) A written composition of moderate length, exploring a particular issue or subject.
A test, experiment; an assay.
The act of inviting; solicitation; the requesting of a person's company.
defs.ex: an invitation to a party, to a dinner, or to visit a friend

defs.d: A document or verbal message conveying an invitation.
defs.ex: We need to print off fifty invitations for the party.

defs.d: A composition, normally in prose, telling a story and intended to be represented by actors impersonating the characters and speaking the dialogue
Such a work for television, radio or the cinema (usually one that is not a comedy)
An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
defs.ex: The horse gave two quick stamps and rose up on its hind legs.

defs.d: An indentation, imprint, or mark made by stamping.
defs.ex: My passport has quite a collection of stamps.

defs.d: To step quickly and heavily, once or repeatedly.
defs.ex: The toddler screamed and stamped, but still got no candy.

defs.d: To move (the foot or feet) quickly and heavily, once or repeatedly.
defs.ex: The crowd cheered and stamped their feet in appreciation.

defs.d: An individual who is not happy.
Not happy; sad.
Not satisfied; unsatisfied.
defs.ex: An unhappy customer is unlikely to return to your shop.

defs.d: A feeling of discomfort or vexation caused by what one dislikes.
That which causes such a feeling.
To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to bother with unpleasant deeds.
defs.ex: Marc loved his sister, but when she annoyed him he wanted to switch her off.

defs.d: To do something to upset or anger someone; to be troublesome.
An act of folding.
defs.ex: After two reraises in quick succession, John realised his best option was probably a fold.

defs.d: A bend or crease.
To bend (any thin material, such as paper) over so that it comes in contact with itself.
To make the proper arrangement (in a thin material) by bending.
defs.ex: If you fold the sheets, they'll fit more easily in the drawer.

defs.d: A history, a non-fiction account of the past.
A historian.
Very important; noteworthy: having importance or significance in history.
defs.ex: A historic opportunity

defs.d: Old-fashioned, untouched by modernity.
Of, concerning, or in accordance with recorded history, (particularly) as opposed to legends, myths, and fictions.
defs.ex: July 4, 1776, is a historic date. A great deal of historical research has been done on the events leading up to that day.

defs.d: Of, concerning, or in accordance with the past generally.
An attitude or a feeling of distaste or aversion.
(usually in the plural) Something that a person dislikes (has or feels aversion to).
defs.ex: Tell me your likes and dislikes.

defs.d: To displease; to offend. (In third-person only.)
To have a feeling of aversion or antipathy towards; not to like.
Something that is owned.
defs.ex: Important types of property include real property (land), personal property (other physical possessions), and intellectual property (rights over artistic creations, inventions, etc.).

defs.d: A piece of real estate, such as a parcel of land.
defs.ex: There is a large house on the property.

defs.d: To invest with properties, or qualities.
To make a property of; to appropriate.
Not at war or disturbed by strife or turmoil.
defs.ex: peaceful protest

defs.d: Inclined to peace.
Something constructed from parts.
defs.ex: Loops and conditional statements are constructs in computer programming.

defs.d: A concept or model.
defs.ex: Bohr's theoretical construct of the atom was soon superseded by quantum mechanics.

defs.d: To build or form (something) by assembling parts.
defs.ex: We constructed the radio from spares.

defs.d: To build (a sentence, an argument, etc.) by arranging words or ideas.
defs.ex: A sentence may be constructed with a subject, verb and object.

defs.d: A living creature.
The state or fact of existence, consciousness, or life, or something in such a state.
Given that; since.
Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
defs.ex: After you hand in your essays, I will give both grades and feedback.

defs.d: (control theory) The part of an output signal that is looped back into the input to control or modify a system.
To generate the high-frequency sound by allowing a speaker to cause vibration of the sound generator of a musical instrument connected by an amplifier to the speaker.
defs.ex: The show ended with a riot of feedbacking guitars.

defs.d: To provide informational feedback to.
defs.ex: His employees feedbacked him a lot more than he wanted.

defs.d: The act or process of dividing anything.
Each of the separate parts of something resulting from division.
Riches; valuable material possessions.
A great amount; an abundance or plenty.
defs.ex: She brings a wealth of knowledge to the project.
